fruits.extendedStory: The number worth remembering here is not the height but the level: 0.3 metres above the sea. That is all that lies between this building and the water. Its story begins in 828, and building went on for centuries, among others under Domenico I Contarini. The style is Romanesque, with round arches and heavy walls. It is dedicated to Mark the Evangelist, whose sign is the winged lion.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Zahl, die man sich merken sollte, ist nicht die Höhe, sondern die Höhenlage: 0,3 Meter über dem Meer. So knapp liegt dieses Haus über dem Wasser. Die Geschichte beginnt 828, gebaut wurde über Jahrhunderte weiter, unter anderem unter Domenico I. Contarini. Der Stil ist romanisch, mit runden Bögen und schweren Mauern. Geweiht ist sie Markus, dem Evangelisten, dessen Zeichen der geflügelte Löwe ist.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The number worth remembering here is not the height but the level: 0.3 metres above the sea. That is all that lies between this building and the water. Its story begins in 828, and building went on for centuries, among others under Domenico I Contarini. The style is Romanesque, with round arches and heavy walls. It is dedicated to Mark the Evangelist, whose sign is the winged lion.

localizedStory.de: Die Kirche steht 0,3 Meter über dem Meer. Ihre Geschichte reicht bis 828 zurück.
localizedStory.en: The church stands 0.3 metres above the sea. Its story goes back to 828.

fruits.name: Basilica di San Marco
fruits.story: The church stands 0.3 metres above the sea. Its story goes back to 828.

fruits.extendedStory: This house belonged to no family. The Republic of Venice commissioned it and owned it, and the doge, the city's elected head, lived in it. Building began in 1340, in the Gothic style. Open arcades run along the bottom and a solid wall sits on top. It looks as though somebody set the building down upside down. Fire took hold three times, in 1483, 1547 and 1577, and three times the work carried on.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Das Haus gehörte nicht einer Familie, sondern der Republik Venedig, und sie gab es auch in Auftrag. Bewohnt wurde es vom Dogen, dem gewählten Oberhaupt der Stadt. Der Bau begann 1340, in Gotik: unten offene Bogengänge, oben eine geschlossene Wand. Das ist herum, als hätte jemand das Gebäude verkehrt aufgestellt. Dreimal brannte es, 1483, 1547 und 1577, und dreimal wurde weitergebaut.
localizedExtendedStory.en: This house belonged to no family. The Republic of Venice commissioned it and owned it, and the doge, the city's elected head, lived in it. Building began in 1340, in the Gothic style. Open arcades run along the bottom and a solid wall sits on top. It looks as though somebody set the building down upside down. Fire took hold three times, in 1483, 1547 and 1577, and three times the work carried on.

localizedStory.de: Der Palast des Dogen, in Auftrag gegeben von der Republik Venedig selbst.
localizedStory.en: The palace of the doge, commissioned by the Republic of Venice itself.

fruits.name: Palazzo Ducale
fruits.story: The palace of the doge, commissioned by the Republic of Venice itself.

fruits.extendedStory: A tower of 98.6 metres, above a city as flat as a plate. That is why it shows from everywhere. Its history starts around the year 1000. What stands there now was raised again by Luca Beltrami, stone by stone on the old pattern. Its name comes from the basilica beside it. From ground level it reads as slender. Tip your head right back and the height arrives all at once.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Ein Turm von 98,6 Metern, und die Stadt darunter liegt flach wie ein Teller. Deshalb sieht man ihn von überall. Seine Geschichte beginnt um das Jahr 1000. Was heute dort steht, richtete Luca Beltrami wieder auf, Stein für Stein nach altem Vorbild. Benannt ist der Turm nach dem Markusdom, neben dem er steht. Von unten wirkt er schmal. Erst wenn man den Kopf ganz in den Nacken legt, merkt man die Höhe.
localizedExtendedStory.en: A tower of 98.6 metres, above a city as flat as a plate. That is why it shows from everywhere. Its history starts around the year 1000. What stands there now was raised again by Luca Beltrami, stone by stone on the old pattern. Its name comes from the basilica beside it. From ground level it reads as slender. Tip your head right back and the height arrives all at once.

localizedStory.de: 98,6 Meter Backstein über dem Markusplatz. Der Turm ist nach der Kirche benannt, neben der er steht.
localizedStory.en: 98.6 metres of brick standing over a city that lies flat as a plate.

fruits.name: Campanile di San Marco
fruits.story: 98.6 metres of brick standing over a city that lies flat as a plate.

fruits.extendedStory: Gian Antonio Selva began building in 1790, and the house opened in 1792. They named it for the phoenix, the bird that rises again out of its own ashes. Twice the building has had to make good on that name. It burned in 1836 and stood again in 1837. It burned once more in 1996 and was rebuilt by 2003. What you are looking at is a theatre that took its own name seriously.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Gian Antonio Selva begann 1790 mit dem Bau, 1792 wurde eröffnet. Den Namen wählte man nach dem Phönix, dem Vogel, der aus seiner Asche wieder aufsteigt. Zweimal musste das Haus diesen Namen einlösen. 1836 brannte es, 1837 stand es wieder. 1996 brannte es erneut, und 2003 war es wieder aufgebaut. Wer heute davorsteht, sieht ein Gebäude, das seinen eigenen Namen ernst genommen hat.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Gian Antonio Selva began building in 1790, and the house opened in 1792. They named it for the phoenix, the bird that rises again out of its own ashes. Twice the building has had to make good on that name. It burned in 1836 and stood again in 1837. It burned once more in 1996 and was rebuilt by 2003. What you are looking at is a theatre that took its own name seriously.

localizedStory.de: Benannt nach dem Phönix, dem Vogel, der aus der Asche steigt. Der Name hat sich zweimal bewahrheitet.
localizedStory.en: Named after the phoenix, the bird that rises from its ashes. The name has come true twice.

fruits.name: Teatro La Fenice
fruits.story: Named after the phoenix, the bird that rises from its ashes. The name has come true twice.

fruits.extendedStory: Teodoro Correr, an art collector from an old Venetian family, left the city his works. He added the palazzo they were kept in, plus money to keep the collection growing. From 1830 it was a museum anyone could enter. In 1922 it moved into the Napoleonic Wing on St Mark's Square, where it sits today. So you walk through one person's collection, which now belongs to everybody.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Teodoro Correr, Kunstsammler aus einer alten venezianischen Familie, hinterließ der Stadt seine Werke. Dazu den Palazzo, in dem sie standen, und Geld, damit die Sammlung weiterwächst. 1830 wurde daraus ein Museum für alle. 1922 zog es in den Napoleonischen Flügel am Markusplatz, wo es bis heute liegt. Man geht also durch die Sammlung eines einzelnen Menschen, die inzwischen der Stadt gehört.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Teodoro Correr, an art collector from an old Venetian family, left the city his works. He added the palazzo they were kept in, plus money to keep the collection growing. From 1830 it was a museum anyone could enter. In 1922 it moved into the Napoleonic Wing on St Mark's Square, where it sits today. So you walk through one person's collection, which now belongs to everybody.

localizedStory.de: Ein Sammler vermachte der Stadt alles: seine Werke, sein Haus und Geld zum Weitersammeln.
localizedStory.en: A collector left the city everything: his works, his house, and money to keep collecting.

fruits.name: Museo Correr
fruits.story: A collector left the city everything: his works, his house, and money to keep collecting.

fruits.extendedStory: The engineer Eugenio Miozzi put up this wooden crossing in just 37 days. It was meant to stand for a while and no longer. It opened in 1933 and never went away. Its arch reaches 48 metres across the Grand Canal in one go. Between 1984 and 1986 it was rebuilt to a design by Giulio Ballio, Giuseppe Creazza, Luciano Jogna and Giancarlo Turrini. The name comes from the picture collection on the bank, the Gallerie dell'Accademia.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Ingenieur Eugenio Miozzi stellte diesen Holzübergang in nur 37 Tagen hin. Er sollte nur eine Weile stehen. 1933 wurde er eröffnet, und weg ist er nie gekommen. Sein Bogen greift in einem Zug 48 Meter über den Canal Grande. Zwischen 1984 und 1986 wurde er nach einem Entwurf von Giulio Ballio, Giuseppe Creazza, Luciano Jogna und Giancarlo Turrini neu gebaut. Der Name stammt von der Gemäldesammlung am Ufer, den Gallerie dell'Accademia.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The engineer Eugenio Miozzi put up this wooden crossing in just 37 days. It was meant to stand for a while and no longer. It opened in 1933 and never went away. Its arch reaches 48 metres across the Grand Canal in one go. Between 1984 and 1986 it was rebuilt to a design by Giulio Ballio, Giuseppe Creazza, Luciano Jogna and Giancarlo Turrini. The name comes from the picture collection on the bank, the Gallerie dell'Accademia.

localizedStory.de: In 37 Tagen aus Holz gebaut, als Übergang für kurze Zeit. Er steht bis heute.
localizedStory.en: Built of wood in 37 days, as a crossing for the time being. It is still there.

fruits.name: Ponte dell'Accademia
fruits.story: Built of wood in 37 days, as a crossing for the time being. It is still there.

fruits.extendedStory: The descendants of doge Enrico Dandolo had this house built in the 13th century. Around 1670 it passed to the Farsetti family, who gave it its name. In the 18th century they turned it into a kind of cultural centre, open to thinkers, artists, citizens and foreign visitors alike. The city bought it in 1826 and made it the town hall the year after. It still is one, together with Ca' Loredan next door.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Nachfahren des Dogen Enrico Dandolo ließen dieses Haus im 13. Jahrhundert bauen. Um 1670 kam es an die Familie Farsetti, die ihm den Namen gab. Im 18. Jahrhundert machten sie eine Art Kulturzentrum daraus, offen für Denker, Künstler, Bürger und Reisende aus dem Ausland. 1826 kaufte es die Stadt und machte es im Jahr darauf zum Rathaus. Das ist es bis heute, zusammen mit der Ca' Loredan nebenan.

It still is one, together with Ca' Loredan next door.

localizedStory.de: Ein Palast aus dem 13. Jahrhundert, gebaut von den Nachfahren eines Dogen. Heute ist er das Rathaus.
localizedStory.en: A palace from the 13th century, built by a doge's descendants. Today it is the town hall.

fruits.extendedStory: The monument in the middle remembers the playwright Carlo Goldoni. Antonio Dal Zotto made it in 1883. The square lies a few steps from the Rialto and counts as the social and commercial heart of the city. It is busy to match. Look towards the Rialto bridge for a half-hidden church front. That is San Bartolomeo, once San Demetrio, from the 12th century.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Das Denkmal in der Mitte erinnert an den Theaterdichter Carlo Goldoni. Antonio Dal Zotto schuf es 1883. Der Platz liegt wenige Schritte vom Rialto entfernt und gilt als das gesellschaftliche und geschäftliche Herz der Stadt. Entsprechend voll ist er. Richtung Rialtobrücke erkennt man halb verdeckt die Fassade der Kirche San Bartolomeo, früher San Demetrio, aus dem 12. Jahrhundert.

localizedStory.de: In der Mitte steht Carlo Goldoni in Bronze, den Stock in der Hand, mitten im Gedränge.
localizedStory.en: Carlo Goldoni stands in the middle in bronze, cane in hand, right in the crush.
